subject: Culture
title: The Roots of Shame
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Roots of Shame.

hook.text: Ancient Greek warriors feared disgrace more than death. Dying in battle was glory; fleeing was ruin.

buildup.text: Shame likely evolved as a social policing tool. Groups that shamed free-riders cooperated better.

discovery.text: Neuroscience confirms shame activates the same brain region as physical pain—the anterior insula.

twist.text: Children as young as two show shame responses. It appears before they can even name the feeling.

climax.text: Shame isn't cultural decoration. It's a survival circuit wired into our brain's threat system.

punchline.text: We feel shame before we understand it.

quiz.question: Which brain region activates during shame?
